name: Lip blushing (cosmetic tattoo)

lead: Lip blushing is a cosmetic tattoo that deposits pigment in the lips for a soft, even tint. People on looksmaxxing forums consider it when they have uneven lip color and find tinted balm wears off quickly.
No trials have measured how it affects appearance. The published literature is mainly case reports of complications.

paras: Pigment is placed in the dermis of the lips by tattooing, so the color is not removed by washing and fades gradually over time.

Reported problems include allergic and granulomatous reactions, infection risk with unsterile equipment, a case of squamous cell carcinomas arising in a lip tattoo, and difficult removal. Forum posters also mention cost and the possibility of an artificial look.

lead: Lip blushing is a form of cosmetic tattooing, also called permanent makeup or micropigmentation, in which pigment is placed in the skin of the lips to add or even out color and soften the lip border [1]. In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed as a semi-permanent alternative to tinted lip balm for people who describe their lip color as uneven or pale [2].

Cosmetic tattooing in general dates to the early twentieth century, with lip tattooing described as a fashion since the early 1930s [1]. Dermatology literature on lip tattoos consists mainly of case reports and reviews of complications, including allergic and granulomatous reactions, and of reports on removal [3][4][5][6][7].
No controlled trials of lip blushing for appearance have been identified. Published evidence on its effects is limited to case reports and case series, mostly describing adverse reactions.
infobox: Lip tint tattoo, micropigmentation, permanent lip color

paras: Permanent makeup uses tattooing to deposit pigment in the dermis so the skin appears made up. Applications include eyeliner, eyebrows and lip color, and it is also used for scar camouflage and areola restoration after breast surgery [1]. Lip blushing refers to a soft, sheer wash of color across the lips, as opposed to a defined lip-liner outline. The Wikipedia article on permanent makeup does not discuss the lip blush style specifically [1].
Results vary with skin tone, pigment and sun exposure, and the article on permanent makeup notes that colors can fade or look different than intended [1].

Common short-term effects of cosmetic tattooing include itching, redness and mild swelling. Less common reactions listed include allergy to pigments, infection, granulomas and keloids, and unsterile equipment can transmit blood-borne disease [1]. Rare reports describe swelling or burning at cosmetic tattoos during MRI [1].

Case reports specific to the lips include a granulomatous reaction appearing four years after a lip tattoo that resolved spontaneously [3], allergic reactions to red lip tattoo pigment treated with hydroxychloroquine [4], a possible flare of such an allergy after SARS-CoV-2 vaccination [5], lymphoid hyperplasia treated with topical tacrolimus [6], a fixed drug eruption localized over a red lip tattoo [7], and eruptive keratoacanthoma-type squamous cell carcinomas arising in a lip tattoo [8].

Removal of cosmetic tattoos can be difficult. Authors report that some pigments, including white or metallic-containing ones, may darken on laser exposure. One report described a lip tattoo that darkened after Q-switched laser hair removal and then improved spontaneously [9], and an older report described a cosmetic tattoo that did not respond to a Q-switched alexandrite laser [10].
No studies found of lip blushing's effect on appearance or satisfaction. The published literature consists of case reports of complications and removal [3][4][5][6][7][8][9][10].

lore.intro: On looksmax.org the procedure is raised by users who want more even or redder lips and are weighing cost and the risk of a result that looks artificial [2][11].

claims.claim: A lip blush tattoo can permanently even out uneven lip color.
If it looks fake on a man, the result is ruined.
Lip color is a key contrasting feature of the face.

timeline.event: Early documented cosmetic tattooing in London by Sutherland MacDonald [1].
Lip tattooing becomes a fashion; tattooist George Burchett helps develop the technique [1].
Permanent makeup becomes much more common, mainly for hair and pigment loss [1].
